MINUTES, JULY 19, 2016. President Philippart called the meeting to order at 5:32 p.m.; present besides Dr. Philippart were Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Schmidt and Underwood, with Mr. Miletti absent. Deputy Superintendent for Teaching & Learning Mark Dziatczak sat in for Superintendent Machesky; administrators Griffor, Harris and West and three members of the audience attended; adjournment 6:43 p.m. Resolution 16-063 (moved Hauff, supported Fleming) approved consent items A-G: minutes of the June 7, June 14 and June 21, 2016 special and regular meetings, plus the Treasurer's Report - May 2016. Resolution 16-064 (Schmidt/Edmunds) approved new hires Sabrina Stevanovic, LaDonna Hunter, Jennifer Erff, Sarah Nunez, Amanda Guibord, Erika Conklin, Anne Gallagher and Christina Rick. Resolution 16-065 (Edmunds/Fleming) extended administrative contracts through June 30, 2018 without tenure in the administrative position and subject to the layoff provision in the Administrative Handbook, covering principals including Lara Dixon (Athens High), Remo Roncone (Troy High), Joe Duda (Larson), Timothy Fulcher (Smith) and Audra Melton (Baker), assistant principals, and directors including Rob Carson (Maintenance and Operations), Stephanie Trotter (Finance) and Kris Young (Technology). Resolution 16-066 (Schmidt/Underwood) enrolled the district's six secondary schools in the Michigan High School Athletic Association, Inc., adopting its Constitution, By-Laws and current HANDBOOK as minimum standards, effective August 1, 2016 through July 31, 2017. Resolution 16-067 (Fleming/Schmidt) approved an Athens High School/Troy High School cooperative team in Boys' and Girls' Skiing for 2016-17 and 2017-18, Athens lacking enough students for its own team under MHSAA regulations. All five carried Yes 6 / No 0 with Miletti absent. Under Other, Dr. Philippart reported the Board Policy Committee's first meeting with Lusk Albertson, completion of the first two sections of the Policy Book, a question about a policy related to gender identity, and a full-Board policy workshop on August 24th or in September. Signed Paula Fleming, Secretary.

AGENDA ITEM 6.A - PERSONNEL. Probationary contracts for the 2016-2017 school year are recommended for Caitlin Sarnowski (1.0 speech-language pathologist, Services Building), Stephanie Collins (1.0 third grade, Bemis), Zachary Downer (1.0 special education resource room, Athens High), Adam Cable (1.0 band, Athens High), Christa Formberg (1.0 speech-language pathologist, Services Building), Sairey Pickering (1.0 English, IA East), Briana Carten (1.0 special education cognitive impairment, Athens High), Barbara Larkin (1.0 GSRP teacher, Troy Union), Gail Hosner (1.0 special education resource room, Troy High), Amanda McCormack (.80 social worker, Services Building), Sarah Condne (.7 life skills/home living, Larson Middle and Troy High), Lynne Krutty (.50 Spanish, IA East), Maureen Gumbel (1.0 social worker, Barnard Elementary and Athens High), Abeer Afana (.8 science, Boulan and Smith Middle), Crystal Geiser (1.0 social worker, Troy Union and Wass) and Melissa McCarty (.5 history, IA East).

AGENDA ITEM 6.B - ADMINISTRATIVE APPOINTMENT. Mr. John Pagel is recommended as Principal of Martell Elementary School on a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure in the administrative position, effective August 17, 2016. He has a 25-year career in education, beginning as a fourth and fifth grade teacher in the Algonac School District, then middle school Assistant Principal in the Avondale School District, and most recently 16 years as principal at Deerfield Elementary in Avondale. He holds a Bachelor's Degree in Elementary Education from The University of Michigan and a Masters of Arts in Educational Administration from Wayne State University.

AGENDA ITEM 7.A - SCHOOLS OF CHOICE, SECTION 105c. Michigan law requires a resolution each school year for districts intending to participate in a Schools of Choice program. Under Section 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979, as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996, the Board would accept applications for the 2017-2018 school year for 90 non-resident 9th grade students attending a school district in another county, provided that intermediate school district is contiguous with the Oakland Intermediate School District boundaries, to attend the International Academy East program located in the Troy School District. IA East enrollment totals run 116, 240, 342, 441, 451, 475, 504, 533 and 564 for the years 2008-2009 through 2016-2017, with 2016-2017 grade counts of 158, 155, 135 and 116 and a four-year percent decrease of 18%. Lottery information for the class of 2020 lists 80 Troy School District seats against 167 applicants, reaching #151 on the wait list, and 90 out-of-county school-of-choice seats against 172 applicants with 78 seats filled. The recommendation is no change to the lottery process for the class of 2021. If classes of 155 to 170 continue, approximately 0.8 to 1.0 additional FTE will be needed for 2017-2018 to support the increase of seniors from the current 116 to 135.

**FY2016 audit**
David R. Youngstrom, CPA, audit partner at Yeo & Yeo, reports an unmodified opinion for June 30, 2016. Total governmental fund balance is $39,803,502 on total assets of $59,241,585; the General Fund closes at $21,532,285 and the 2014 Capital Projects Fund at $12,116,251. General Fund revenues are 67% state ($94,326,224) and 26% local ($36,089,115); expenditures are 50% salaries ($69,886,143) and 32% benefits ($45,161,032). The governance letter cites a material weakness in capitalized assets; the Nutrition Cluster draws a qualified opinion with a material weakness for excess fund balance, while the Special Education Cluster is unmodified. Future challenges include a pension obligation over $206 million.

**Item 8.D - Adair litigation.** The Board is asked to rescind its action of May 12, 1998 and withdraw as a participant in the Adair lawsuit against the State of Michigan over underfunding of state-mandated services, effective October 18, 2016, because recent rulings have not been favorable. An attached confidential October 1, 2016 letter from Dennis R. Pollard of Secrest Wardle, 2600 Troy Center Drive, P.O. Box 5025, Troy, MI 48007-5025, 248-851-9500, reports that the Court of Appeals dismissed the appeal in its entirety on September 20, 2016 and that the Liaison Committee authorized seeking leave to appeal to the Michigan Supreme Court on a single issue: the Legislature's practice of adopting a categorical appropriation while concurrently reducing other appropriations to the same local units. The letter recounts the 1997 decision holding special education services mandated under the Headlee Amendment, the resulting dollar-for-dollar deduction and "three bucket funding scheme," and the 2010 decision on the Center for Educational Performance and Information (CEPI), after which the Legislature adopted School Aid Act Section 152a in 2011 with an equal offsetting reduction in each district's general operating revenues. It quotes Article 9, Section 25, cites Section 29, and sets a deadline of November 1, 2016 to submit the application for leave.
